newsitem.title: CANADA: Hearings open on Sable Island natural gas project.
newsitem.headline: Hearings open on Sable Island natural gas project.

text.p: Regulators opened lengthy hearings on Monday on the proposed C$3 billion Sable Island Offshore Energy Project and the thorny issue of whether the natural gas should be shipped via Quebec.

The National Energy Board (NEB) panel took under advisement a motion by the Ecology Action Centre to adjourn the hearing process. Energy industry representatives are expected to oppose the motion in hearings on Tuesday.

Project backers want to drill in six fields in the Atlantic Ocean 200 kms east of Nova Scotia. It is believed to be one of North America's largest undeveloped gas deposits with reserves of 3 trillion cubic feet.
The project is lead by Mobil Oil Canada and includes Shell Canada Ltd, Imperial Oil Ltd and Nova Scotia Resources Ltd.

The proposal also calls for constructing the Maritimes and Northeast Pipeline that would ship the gas through Nova Scotia, New Brunswick and Maine to southern New England. Martimes and Northeast will be owned by Mobil, Westcoast Energy Inc and PanEnergy Corp.

The NEB panel will also hear evidence from the competing Trans-Quebec and Maritimes pipeline (TQM) proposal that calls for shipping the gas to Montreal before it goes to the United States. TQM is owned by TransCanada PipeLines Ltd and Gaz Metropolitain and Co LP.

The battle over the pipeline routee has taken on political overtones. Prime Minister Jean Chretien and Quebec officials both favor the TQM route, while Nova Scotia provincial leaders have spoken in favor of the Maritimes and Northeast plan.

The hearings will continue until late May when the panel will decide if it will need more evidence on the issue. The NEB is expected to issue a recommendation to the federal government in early fall. If approved, the gas could be flowing by November 1999.
The U.S. sections of both pipelines will also have to be reviewed by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, which hinted last summer it would let the market decide which project will go forward.
